verification_report.summary: The two supplied supplements pass strict sequential verification against the cited checkpoint41 sources and the completed root-tail/current-attainment and trace-saturation audits. For the tail proposition, the compact-current uniform-integrability result, exact smooth-test/current supremum, and uniform-tail closure criterion have the stated hypotheses. The proof correctly preserves the quantifier order for an arbitrary fixed perturbation bound, selects smooth near-optimal tests when tails fail, uses regularity of each finite p k_T dV measure to obtain compact tail cores and small-volume open neighborhoods, constructs smooth cutoffs, and proves L1 convergence of the actual densities by absolute continuity of the p^n integral. For the divisorial proposition, the subsolution threshold, smooth-test trace inequality, and Poincare–Lelong/Stokes calculation are applied only with smooth dd^c-closed tests. The divisor’s smooth-volume-null support supplies the additive trace mass. The proof establishes 0≤kappa<1 before exponentiation and derives c≤b(1-kappa)^n. At c=b it proves zero beta_E pairing for smooth-test clusters, excludes bigness through the ordinary closed Bott–Chern threshold, and invokes near-maximizer convergence only under the stated root-tail hypothesis. The face is correctly confined to the weak closure of smooth normalized Gauduchon forms, shown nonempty only at c=b, and is not confused with the full current set. No geometric realization, exact equation, unrestricted singular-current product, BMP, positive-lower-mass, null-locus, or novelty conclusion is added. The submission contains no external-paper citation, so no arXiv/web fallback was required.
